content:
This August, Fender launched the MIX wireless headphones, priced at US$299. These over-ear headphones feature replaceable batteries and a FWD Tx USB-C wireless transmitter, offering low-latency, lossless connection quality. Fender MIX headphones can now also be tuned via an iPhone app, allowing users to adjust their listening experience according to personal preference.

The Fender Audio iPhone app provides EQ presets and a customisable five-band equaliser, allowing users to independently adjust the bass, low-mid, mid, high-mid and treble frequency bands, fine-tuning the sound directly within the iPhone app to suit their personal taste.

The app also features a battery indicator and customisable home screen widgets for quick access to functions such as EQ settings.

As for the headphones themselves, the MIX uses 40mm graphene drivers, hybrid active noise cancellation and Bluetooth 5.3. Fender says battery life is up to 52 hours with active noise cancellation enabled; with ANC off, it can reach 100 hours.

The included USB-C transmitter supports multiple modes, including lossless audio up to 24-bit/96kHz, low-latency listening, and Auracast broadcasting to multiple compatible devices.

The headphones can also be used wired via USB-C or a 3.5mm audio cable.

After an initial listen, I found that with active noise cancellation enabled, the MIX delivers quite solid sound quality. However, when switching to Fender's transparency mode (ambient sound), the audio quality noticeably drops for me—at least when not using the transmitter and connecting via Bluetooth only.

I'm looking forward to trying the app's EQ controls so I can tune the sound closer to my personal taste.

When not in use, the USB-C transmitter can be stored behind the ear cup; if convenience takes priority over sound quality, you can also simply connect via Bluetooth directly.

The Fender Audio app is now available on the App Store, supporting Fender MIX headphones.
